audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL-focused specifications: secp256r1 precompile (EIP-7951), Merkle Patricia Trie operations, BN128 precompiles, transaction receipt status codes (EIP-658), and Arrow Glacier difficulty bomb delay.

misclassified_entities.reason: Smart contracts invoking precompiles are internal to the EVM execution environment. They execute within the EL, not outside it.
ZK proof verifier contracts are smart contracts executing within the EVM. They are internal to the EL.
Calling contracts are internal EVM entities, not external to the system boundary.
Key providers for trie operations are internal EL components (e.g., transaction processing, state management). Keys are derived internally.

This represents calldata within the EVM, which originates from internal contract calls. The actual untrusted input enters at the transaction submission boundary, already captured as EXT-TX-SUBMITTER-RPC.
Duplicate of EXT-TX-SUBMITTER-RPC from batch 1. Transaction senders interact via JSON-RPC, already modeled.

trusted_external_entities.name: WebAuthn/FIDO2 Device via Smart Contract
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: secp256r1 precompile (0x100) calldata containing device-generated signatures
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Signatures from WebAuthn/FIDO2 hardware devices enter the EL as transaction calldata routed to the secp256r1 precompile. The device itself is external to the Ethereum system. All signature data must be fully validated: input length (160 bytes), signature bounds (0 < r,s < n), public key bounds (0 <= qx,qy < p), curve equation verification, and point-at-infinity check. No trust is placed in the signature content.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via P2P Protocol
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P block propagation (block headers with difficulty)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Reconfirmed from batch 1. Peers propagate blocks whose difficulty must be independently validated against Arrow Glacier rules (bomb offset 10,700,000). Invalid difficulty blocks must be rejected.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Miner/Validator)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Block header fields and transaction receipt generation
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Reconfirmed from batch 1. Block producers set difficulty values and transaction execution determines receipt status codes. Difficulty is verified by all validating nodes. Receipt status is deterministic from execution.

trusted_external_entities.name: RPC Client via eth_getTransactionReceipt
trusted_external_entities.rationale: RPC clients query transaction receipts. Read-only queries but must be rate-limited to prevent DoS. Receipt data is read from local state and returned.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All cryptographic input must be validated before use: input length exactly 160 bytes, signature components r and s in range (0, n), public key coordinates within field modulus, point on curve, point not at infinity. Gas (6900) consumed regardless of validation outcome to prevent DoS. Signature malleability is not prevented by the precompile; applications must handle this.

Block difficulty must be recomputed independently using the correct fork's difficulty formula (Arrow Glacier: bomb offset 10,700,000). Claimed difficulty must match computed expected difficulty exactly. Blocks with mismatched difficulty must be rejected.

Read-only operation returning receipt data from local state. Transaction hash input must be validated for format. Response must correctly reflect post-Byzantium status code format (0 = failure, 1 = success).

Difficulty set by block producer must be validated against the difficulty formula. For Arrow Glacier, the bomb delay offset of 10,700,000 must be correctly applied. Receipt status codes are deterministic from execution and cannot be manipulated independently.
